storyTagline: The Eagles lose 4 games and win a sixth straight title anyway, 40-26 over the Bengals in Super Bowl CLV, Ryland Maxwell and Akiem Brock retire into the Hall of Fame, and Grover Calitro scores 43 times.

stories.headline: Six Straight: Eagles Beat the Bengals 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV
stories.dek: Philadelphia lost 4 regular-season games, its most under Dorren Skura, and still won a sixth straight title as Ryland Maxwell took a 7th Super Bowl MVP in his final season.

stories.headline: Mad Max Signs Off: 2,574 Yards, a 7th Super Bowl MVP and the Hall of Fame
stories.dek: Ryland Maxwell's last season was one of his best. He retires with 32,108 career rushing yards, 13 rings and the highest Career Legacy on file.

stories.headline: Akiem Brock Walks Away With 8 Rings and a First-Ballot Plaque
stories.dek: The league's best blocker made 62 blocks in his final season, and he and Ryland Maxwell are the Hall of Fame's Class of Y96.

stories.headline: Leglue's MVP at 36 Is a Verdict on Crawford's 17 Interceptions
stories.dek: Bones Crawford threw 52 touchdown passes, 11 more than anyone, and led the league in interceptions for a third straight season. The award went to Detroit.

stories.headline: Calitro's 43 Touchdowns Break the Season Mark and Carry Cincinnati to the Final
stories.dek: Grover Calitro passed Siran Spector's 42 for the most rushing touchdowns in a season on file, and Alshon Lazard found his game again. The Bengals fell 40-26 in Super Bowl CLV.

stories.headline: Brooker Draws Level With Hobbs at 43, and Swaim Climbs to Third on the Tackle List
stories.dek: Jamon Brooker tied the career interception record, Lewis Pettis was shut out, and Ryland Maxwell retired 4 rushing touchdowns short of second place.

stories.headline: Ty Lock's Long Goodbye, and the Rookie Who Took His Place
stories.dek: The Giants' quarterback since Y83 is retired after 330 games and 627 touchdown passes. Yurik Okudah threw 34 in his first season.

stories.headline: Rashawn Elder Catches 122 Passes, and the Class of Y95 Keeps Coming
stories.dek: A rookie tight end led the league in catches, Mario Lamb scored 28 times for the Chiefs, and Payton Jarrett has 2 rings in 2 seasons.

takes.headline: Grover Calitro Set the League Record With 43 Rushing Touchdowns and Lost Offensive Player of the Year. Indefensible.
takes.dek: Calitro: 1,904 yards and 43 scores. The winner, Alton Yeldon: 1,558 yards and 27.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Retired 4 Touchdowns Short of Second Place. The Greatest Ever Left Too Early.
takes.dek: 2,574 yards and 25 touchdowns in his last season, and 421 career rushing scores to Lane McCoy's 458.

takes.headline: Margus Leglue's MVP Corrected Last Year's Mistake: 41 Touchdowns and 1 Interception Beats 52 and 17
takes.dek: Bones Crawford threw more touchdowns. Leglue threw 16 fewer interceptions, and the voters finally weighed both.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford's Card Rose 124% in the Year He Lost the MVP. The Market Is Buying a Retirement.
takes.dek: From 8,559 to 19,210 after a season with 17 interceptions, 7 more than the year before.

takes.headline: A.T. Hoyer Matched the Defensive Player of the Year's 237 Tackles in 3 Fewer Games
takes.dek: Abraham Jack needed 20 games for his 237. Hoyer got there in 17, with one more interception.

takes.headline: Jacob Proise's Card Is Up 398% on 786 Yards. Sell It Before Everyone Else Does.
takes.dek: The tight end went from 1,109 to 5,527 while the receiver beside him gained 2,096 yards and 26%.

takes.headline: Ty Lock Threw for 68,237 Yards and the Hall of Fame Said No. The Hall Got It Right.
takes.dek: 2 rings, both with the Jets, then a Giants career from Y83 to Y95 without another.

takes.headline: Six Straight Titles, and the 13-4 Eagles Were the Weakest Champion of the Run
takes.dek: 4 losses, the most since Philadelphia hired Dorren Skura, and still nobody could finish the job.

takes.headline: Jamon Brooker Just Tied the Career Interceptions Record. He Is the Best Player Without a Ring.
takes.dek: 43 interceptions, level with Hall of Famer Damar Hobbs, 2 Defensive Player of the Year awards and a Hall of Fame watch score of 91.

takes.headline: Akiem Brock Went In First Ballot Without a Single Award, and That Is the Hall Working
takes.dek: 8 rings, 181 games, and the highest Career Legacy of any offensive lineman.

didYouKnow.text: Ryland Maxwell retired with 13 rings and 7 Super Bowl MVPs, both the most on file, and Dorren Skura coached him to every one of the rings.
Grover Calitro's 43 rushing touchdowns in Y96 are the most in a season on league cards. Nobody else in the league scored more than 30.
Bones Crawford threw 17 interceptions in Y96. No other quarterback threw more than 6, and Crawford also threw the most touchdown passes, 52.
Rookie tight end Rashawn Elder led the league with 122 catches in Y96 and averaged 5.5 yards a catch.
Jamon Brooker and Damar Hobbs share the career interception record at 43. Brooker was 33 when he drew level.
Akiem Brock made 62 blocks in his final season, 29 more than any other lineman on league cards.
Margus Leglue threw 41 touchdown passes and 1 interception in Y96 and won his first MVP at 36.
Linebacker Snoop Dotson led the league with 4 sacks in Y96 and also intercepted 5 passes.
The Eagles lost 4 regular-season games in Y96, their most under Dorren Skura, and still won a sixth straight Super Bowl.
Travon Swaim is 121 tackles behind K'Lavon Settle's league record for career tackles (3,185): 96% of the way there.

All 24 Defensive Player of the Year awards on league cards belong to defensive backs. The game credits a corner or safety's stop on a pass play as an interception, and the award rating counts each interception as much as 6 tackles. Jayon Queen leads with 2 awards.

Defensive linemen have 104 career interceptions in 9,250 games, one every 89 games; defensive backs pick one off every 9.5 games. The game scores a lineman's stop on a pass play as a sack: linemen have 424 sacks, defensive backs 1.

Retro Bowl rolls injuries only for the coach's own club: at most one new injury a game and at most three players out at once. With rehab facilities at 10, the squad's injuries can add up to at most 5 weeks out at a time. Through Y97 week 0, all 256 tracked players on the other clubs have played every one of their club's games.
Skura's Eagles are the one club the game can injure. Through Y97 week 0, all 8 of their tracked players have played every game, and nobody is injured now.
Retro Bowl caps each draft class by the coach's last record. After Skura's Eagles went 13-4 in Y96 (76.5%), prospects 5 to 50 of the Y97 class could rate at most 3 stars; a .500 season allows 3.5.
Winning shrinks the draft: in 73 of Skura's 78 seasons that fed a draft at the same club, his record capped the next class at 3 stars or less.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Sherman Brandson
vault.text: The General never flinched. Career Legacy 13,596, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Rondale Ikarras
vault.text: Flashy, loud, unstoppable, and he knew it. He was that guy. Career Legacy 11,172, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · God Johnson
vault.text: He changed his name to God. Then he earned it. Career Legacy 12,765, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jayon Queen
vault.text: Two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Only one other player in this league has ever matched that. Career Legacy 8,744, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyrone Baugh
vault.text: Seven seasons, seven championships, and Tyrone Baugh has a ring for every one of them. Career Legacy 8,479, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Levante Hopkins
vault.text: The quiet one who did the dirty work. Career Legacy 11,464, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Mose Junior
vault.text: Some players chase rings. Mose Junior chased ball carriers. Career Legacy 7,748, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Dennis Baylon
vault.text: Seven trips to the Super Bowl. Seven rings. Not one loss. Career Legacy 10,432, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Charlie John
vault.text: Seven straight Super Bowls. Charlie John was there for every one of them. Career Legacy 10,123, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ian Finney
vault.text: The first superstar. The Infinity Man. Career Legacy 11,413, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Bilal Tolbert
vault.text: No individual trophies. Four rings. And a sack record nobody has caught. Career Legacy 8,506, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Wayne Wilson
vault.text: Four hundred thirty-one games. Nobody in this league has played longer. Career Legacy 9,533, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cairo Asanjh
vault.text: Some players chase records. Cairo Asanjh chased Ian Finney. Career Legacy 10,364, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jahmyr Gibbs
vault.text: Mr. Incredible was here at the start, and he set the bar high. Career Legacy 7,527, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Zander Kolar
vault.text: Some defensive linemen are measured in sacks. Zander Kolar was measured in tackles. Career Legacy 8,713, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ray Waller
vault.text: Never count out a man whose nickname is a promise. Career Legacy 8,940, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyler Pacheco
vault.text: Tyler Pacheco never needed the big play. He needed the ball, and he got it. Career Legacy 7,879, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lukas Russell
vault.text: The Running Man started fast and never slowed down. Career Legacy 9,353, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Taron Hayes
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game, for 213 games, and two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Career Legacy 7,152, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Nick Bolton
vault.text: One of the originals, and he never stopped tackling. Career Legacy 8,781, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Michael Wilson
vault.text: Wayne's son, and nobody's afterthought. Career Legacy 8,799, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jackson Wardell Kline
vault.text: Tyrion Kline's son did not live in anyone's shadow. He built his own. Career Legacy 10,135, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Malakai Sawyer
vault.text: Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them. Career Legacy 7,406, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · K'Lavon Settle
vault.text: Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles. Career Legacy 7,759, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Daren Teamer
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game is a Hall of Fame habit, and Daren Teamer has never broken it. Career Legacy 8,285, Y89 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Kalif Suh
vault.text: A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him. Career Legacy 9,305, Y92 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jakeem Friend
vault.text: Linemen do not win trophies. Jakeem Friend won seven rings instead. Career Legacy 9,415, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lane McCoy
vault.text: Every time Denver got close to the goal line, the whole league knew who was getting the ball. Career Legacy 6,390, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Damar Hobbs
vault.text: No defender in league history has taken the ball away through the air more often than Damar Hobbs. Career Legacy 8,423, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ryland Maxwell
vault.text: Thirteen rings, and the first player to win every major award. Career Legacy 14,903, Y96 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Akiem Brock
vault.text: Eight rings, 538 blocks and one club. Career Legacy 11,394, Y96 class.
